title: Industry Information on Recruitment Plans of Employers for Future Jobs
what_it_is: Industry Information on Recruitment Plans of Employers for Future Jobs

sections.label: Industry Transformation Maps and job plans
sections.summary: The Minister was asked whether the Ministry regularly obtains industry recruitment-plan information and would publish it to help the public plan jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower whether the Ministry regularly obtains industry information on recruitment plans of employers for future jobs, especially those involving time spans of three years and beyond, in the major economic sectors and, if so, whether it is prepared to publish such information on a regular basis to assist the general public in making better job plans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: These Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs) outline the key growth areas for each sector and the future profile of skills and jobs that Singaporeans can pursue.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: The ITMs are also accompanied by their respective skills frameworks which outline very specific career paths, occupations, salary range, skills requirements and training programmes available for each of these sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: To date, ITMs have been launched for the Retail, Food Services and Precision Engineering sectors.

sections.label: Forecasting future jobs and skills
sections.summary: The Ministry looks ahead to forecast future jobs and skills, but company-level forecasts three years ahead may be a challenge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Yes, in fact, we are trying to look ahead and make a forecast in terms of future jobs and future skills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: However, to make a forecast at the company level, three years ahead may be a challenge because not many companies are prepared to make that kind of commitment upfront.

sections.label: Place and Train, Train and Place
sections.summary: The passage names two programmes: Place and Train, and Train and Place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: One is Place and Train, the other is Train and Place.

sections.label: Training programmes and employment outcomes
sections.summary: Programmes aim to ensure workers are meaningfully employed after training, with Place and Train for the unemployed and Train and Place for the employed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: This is to ensure that by the time the worker has gone through the training, he/she will be meaningfully employed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: So, most of our programmes are targeted at Place and Train for those not in employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: For those in employment, the focus would be on Train and Place.

sections.label: Strengthening programmes to minimise mismatch
sections.summary: Strengthening Place and Train and Train and Place programmes may minimise the mismatch for professionals, managers, executives and technicians.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: If we can continue to strengthen the Place and Train, and the Train and Place programmes, then, hopefully, we can minimise this mismatch, and the mismatch for professionals, managers, executives and technicians.
